what: Create the private repo RhinoHealth/claude-plugins with a marketplace.json named rhino, folders for the rhino-core, fe-guild, be-guild and devops-guild plugins, and entries for fcp-lab and kb, which live in their own repos.

Layout, reusing agent-skills' plugin layout (its open PR #1): .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (sketch below), plugins/<name>/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/<name>/{skills,agents,commands,hooks,evals}/, scripts/ for CI checks, catalog.yaml, STYLE.md.

title: [Platform] rhino-core: write the plan-and-grill skill
needs: G4: Nova's readiness check and grill step use this skill and post the same plan format
what: The first rhino-core skill: before code, decide whether to ask the requester questions first, then write a one-screen plan with the definition of done, 3–5 checks including an edge case, screen states for UI, the proof each check needs, an estimate, risks and what is out of scope.
why: Most rework starts with a misread ticket. Asking first on big or vague tickets and agreeing the checks before coding is cheaper than a second PR, for people and for Nova.
how: Create plugins/rhino-core/.claude-plugin/plugin.json and skills/plan-and-grill/SKILL.md (sketch below), with references/grill-questions.md that loads only for big or vague tasks.
Write goals, reasons, examples and signs to look for: when a small clear fix skips the grill, what a good check looks at (what the user sees), one worked example each for an FE and a BE ticket.
Match the plan format Nova posts on Jira and Slack (G4), so people and Nova write the same plan.
3 eval cases: a vague ticket gets questions before a plan; a typo fix gets a plan and no grill; the plan names an edge case and the proof for each check.

code.text:
---
name: plan-and-grill
description: "Use before writing code for a ticket or task: decide whether to ask the requester questions first, then write a one-screen plan with the definition of done, 3-5 checks including an edge case, the proof each check needs, an estimate, risks and what is out of scope."
when_to_use: "A Jira ticket, bug report or feature request is about to be built; the user says 'plan this' or 'grill me'; the task is big or vague."
argument-hint: "[Jira key or task description]"
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# plan-and-grill

Goal: agree what "done" means before any code, so the work is checked against the ask, not against itself.

## Ask first, or plan now?
Ask the requester first when the ticket is big, spans teams, or two readings would lead to different code. Signs:
no example, a vague verb ("improve", "support"), a screen with no states, a change to an API others use. A small,
clear fix (a typo, copy, one obvious bug) goes straight to the plan. For big tasks read references/grill-questions.md.

## The plan (one screen)
1. Done means: 1-2 sentences in the user's words.
2. Checks: 3-5, at least one edge case. Each says what it looks at (what the user sees, an API response, a row
   count) and its proof: a short video, screenshots at 760 and 1440, or text output.
3. Screen states for UI: empty, loading, error, long content.
4. Estimate, risks, and what is out of scope.

title: [Platform] rhino-core: write the verify skill and point AGENTS.md to it
needs: G7: npm run verify (new script in frontend/package.json) and poe verify; G6-06: the root CLAUDE.md; G4: the checking guide adds starting checks per kind of change
what: A skill for any code change before saying done: seed fake data, run the area's verify command, look at what the user sees, plant a bug to prove a check can fail, and record proof. One line in fcp's frontend/AGENTS.md and root CLAUDE.md points to it.
why: Proof, not claims: a reviewer should see that each check ran and could have failed. People, Nova and every routine use the same skill, so "done" means the same thing everywhere.
how: skills/verify/SKILL.md (sketch below) and references/per-area.md: FE `npm run verify` (until G7 adds it: npm run lint, npm run check-types, vitest on related files); BE `poe verify` (until then scripts/local_run_backend_unit_tests.sh); FCP Lab with seed data for anything visible (fcp-lab skill, TestDataCreator scenarios).

Cover both outcomes: on pass, record and move on; on fail, it's yours until main's latest run shows the same failure (link it). Fix the code; don't skip, delete or loosen a check, and say in the PR if you think a test is wrong.
Planting a bug: flip one condition or return value in your change, run the check, see it fail, revert, and note what you planted.
Proof: a video up to 30 s for flows, screenshots at 760 and 1440 for layout, text for API calls and CLI output, seed data only, each labelled with its check so pr-story can use it.
Add one line to frontend/AGENTS.md and the root CLAUDE.md: "Before you say a change is done, use the verify skill (rhino-core)." There is no `verify` script in frontend/package.json yet; G7 adds it.
4 eval cases: FE commands for a frontend edit; a planted bug for a new test; it won't delete a failing test; it links main's run when a failure isn't ours.

code.text:
---
name: verify
description: "Use before saying a code change is done: choose checks that prove it works, run the area's verify command, show a new check can fail by planting a bug, and record proof a reviewer can see."
when_to_use: "After editing code, tests or config; when a check fails and you need to know whether it's yours; when filling in 'How it was checked' in a PR."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# verify: proof, not claims

## Where to start
Run the area's verify command (references/per-area.md): `npm run verify` in frontend/, `poe verify` for cloud,
client and sdk. Then check what the user would see: open the flow in FCP Lab with seed data (fcp-lab skill), or
call the API and read the response.

## Signs to look deeper
You changed a serializer, a migration, a proto, a public SDK function or shared UI; there is no test near the
diff; the change is about timing, permissions or time zones.

## Prove a check can fail
Plant a small bug in your change (flip a condition), run the check, watch it fail, revert. If it still passes,
the check doesn't cover your change: write a better one.

## When a check fails
It's yours until main's latest run shows the same failure; then link that run and say so. The answer is to fix
the code, not to skip, delete or loosen the check. If you think a test is wrong, explain why in the PR and leave
the call to the reviewer.

## Record the proof
Per check: the command, pass or fail, and the proof the plan named (a video up to 30 s, screenshots at 760 and
1440, or text). Seed data only.

title: [Shai] Write the skill style guide and catalog.yaml with owners

why: Hard rules about method make strong models worse; goals, reasons and examples work better. A catalog with owners makes sure every skill has someone who keeps its evals green.

code.text:
---
name: pr-story
description: "Use when opening or updating a pull request or posting a Jira ticket update: writes the description with our fixed headings, in plain words for a reviewer from the other team, with the right proof (video, screenshots, a diagram, text, or nothing)."
when_to_use: "gh pr create, gh pr edit, a draft PR becoming ready, or a status comment on a ticket."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# pr-story

A reviewer from the other team should understand this PR in two minutes. Same headings, same order, every time.
Keep the part above the fold under about 300 words; link long output instead of pasting it.

Title: `[FE] RH-1234: what changes for the user` (`[BE]` for backend).

## What changes
1-3 plain sentences about the visible effect.
## Why
The ticket link, and the root cause in one line with file:line.
## How it was checked
Each check from the plan: pass or fail, with its proof labelled by check.
## What was not checked, and why
## Risk and rollback
The risk, how to revert, what to watch after merge.
## Where to look first
2-3 files, and any question for the reviewer.
<details><summary>Receipt, trace and cost</summary>Self-review receipt, trace link, harness suggestions, cost and time.</details>

Pick media with references/media.md. Never pictures of code or logs, never real data.

title: [Platform] Plugin CI: claude plugin validate, skill checks and version bump
needs: G5: Renovate bumps the pinned Claude Code version
what: A workflow in claude-plugins validates the marketplace and every plugin with `claude plugin validate --strict` on each PR, checks skill frontmatter and description limits against catalog.yaml, and fails when a changed plugin's version wasn't bumped.
why: Claude Code updates a plugin only when its version changes, and a broken manifest silently drops a skill on every laptop. These checks are cheap and catch both before merge.
how: .github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml (sketch below), also callable with workflow_call so rnd-kb-tooling (kb) and fcp-local-lab (fcp-lab) run the same checks.

scripts/check_skills.py, adapted from agent-skills' validate_frontmatter.py: name matches its folder; description plus when_to_use under 600 characters (Claude Code truncates at 1,536) and it says when to use the skill; the skill is in catalog.yaml with an owner; 3–10 eval cases under the plugin's evals/<skill>/; a warning on ALL-CAPS MUST, NEVER or CRITICAL.

scripts/check_version_bump.py: a change under plugins/

/ needs a higher version in plugins/

/.claude-plugin/plugin.json than on the base branch.
Pin Claude Code by version; make `plugin-ci / validate` a required check in the ruleset.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml
name: plugin-ci
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_call: {} # rnd-kb-tooling (kb) and fcp-local-lab (fcp-lab) reuse the same checks
permissions:
  contents: read
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest # needs no model access; confirm the runner group with DevOps
    outputs:
      changed_plugins: ${{ steps.changed.outputs.plugins }} # JSON list for the evals job (G8-12); nightly: every plugin
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with: { node-version: 24 }
      - run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.289 # pinned; Renovate bumps it
      - name: Validate the catalogs and every plugin
        run: |
          claude plugin validate . --strict
          claude plugin validate channels/latest --strict
          for plugin in plugins/*/; do claude plugin validate "$plugin" --strict; done
      - name: Skill frontmatter, description limits, owners and eval counts
        run: python3 scripts/check_skills.py --catalog catalog.yaml --min-cases 3 --max-cases 10
      - name: Version bumped for every changed plugin
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        run: python3 scripts/check_version_bump.py --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
      - id: changed
        run: python3 scripts/changed_plugins.py --base "origin/${{ github.base_ref || 'main' }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

title: [Platform] Plugin CI: gitleaks and a high-risk flag for hooks, MCP, scripts
what: Add a secret scan and a risk check to plugin CI. Changes to hooks, .mcp.json, bin/ or scripts/, or to a skill's allowed-tools, get a high-risk label and one comment telling the reviewer what will run on every laptop and agent VM.
why: Hooks, MCP servers and scripts run code on every machine that has the plugin, and allowed-tools skips permission prompts. A Snyk audit found 13% of public skills with critical issues, so these changes need a careful look.
how: Job `secrets`: gitleaks from its pinned release binary over the PR's commits (`gitleaks git --log-opts=origin/main..HEAD --redact --exit-code 1`).

Job `risk` (sketch below): match changed files against the high-risk paths and diff allowed-tools lines in SKILL.md frontmatter; on a match add the high-risk label and post one comment, edited in place on later pushes.
The label informs the one reviewer; it is not an extra approval (exactly 1 approval, no CODEOWNERS). The reviewer runs the plugin locally before approving.
Add to STYLE.md: prefer a skill that runs a CLI over a new MCP server; a new MCP server needs Ronen (Security) and an entry in the managed MCP allow-list (G8-16).

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml (continued)
  risk:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: { contents: read, pull-requests: write }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }
      - name: Find changes that run code or skip prompts on every machine
        id: risk
        run: |
          base="origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"
          git diff --name-only "$base"...HEAD | grep -E '(^|/)(hooks|bin|scripts|monitors)/|\.mcp\.json$' > risky.txt || true
          git diff "$base"...HEAD -- '**/SKILL.md' | grep -E '^[+-](allowed-tools|disallowed-tools):' >> risky.txt || true
          echo "count=$(wc -l < risky.txt | tr -d ' ')" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Label and explain for the reviewer
        if: steps.risk.outputs.count != '0'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
        run: |
          gh pr edit "$PR" --add-label high-risk
          { echo "**High risk:** these changes run code or skip prompts on every laptop and agent VM with this plugin."
            echo "Please run the plugin locally before you approve."
            echo '```'; cat risky.txt; echo '```'; } > comment.md
          gh pr comment "$PR" --body-file comment.md --edit-last --create-if-none

title: [Platform] rhino-core hooks: block secrets and credential files, lint edits
needs: G0/G3: agents' extra walls (locked checks, protected paths) stay in Nova's TypeScript harness hooks (G3-21)
what: Two small hooks in rhino-core: before a write, refuse content that looks like a secret or an edit to a credential file; after an edit, lint that one file and show the result.
why: A secret pasted into a file is the most common leak, and a lint error is cheapest to fix right after the edit. Hooks are enforced, not asked for in a prompt.
how: hooks/hooks.json (sketch below). hooks/guard_write.py checks new content for AWS keys, GitHub and Slack tokens and private key blocks, and paths like .env*, *.pem, id_rsa*, **/secrets/**; it exits 2 with a short reason so Claude sees why. Both hooks are Python 3, stdlib only, unlike the TypeScript agent platform: hooks run straight from the plugin folder on every laptop and VM with no install step, and python3 ships with git's Command Line Tools on every Mac, while Node doesn't.

hooks/lint_after_edit.py: frontend/**/*.ts(x) → `npx biome check <file>`; .py under cloud/, client/ or sdk/ → black --check, isort --check and flake8 with the repo's own config; problems come back as context and never block.
Keep both to one file and a few seconds, and silent when clean.
2 eval cases: writing a fake AWS key is refused; a .tsx edit with a lint error shows the Biome message.

title: [Guilds] Write the fe-codebase skill and its evals
needs: G5: the FE routines load this skill
what: The FE guild writes fe-codebase in the fe-guild plugin: where things live, the design system, data fetching with useQuery, layouts from 760 to 1440 with container queries, Storybook stories per state, e2e page objects with test.step, tests on test IDs, ARIA and text, and the risky areas, with 3–10 eval cases.
why: Nova and the FE routines need the same map a new FE engineer needs. Writing it once, with evals, keeps it honest and lets the monthly diet trim it.
how: Start from frontend/AGENTS.md and the reviewer memory in pr-code-review/references/memory (25 files); link to them instead of copying.
Write signs to look deeper (sketch below), including the guild's own review habits: tests through Storybook stories and not class names; useQuery over useResult.

Eval cases (case.yaml with graders): it fires for a frontend task; a component change gets a story per state; a new e2e flow goes into e2e/pages/*Page.ts with Given/When/Then steps; it stays quiet for a backend task.
Owner: FE guild (catalog.yaml). Run `claude plugin eval plugins/fe-guild` locally before opening the PR.

code.text:
---
name: fe-codebase
description: "Use when working in fcp/frontend: where things live, the design system, data fetching with useQuery, layouts that work from 760 to 1440 px with container queries, Storybook stories per state, e2e page objects with test.step, and the risky areas."
when_to_use: "Any edit, review or plan that touches frontend/ (components, pages, hooks, e2e specs, stories)."
paths: ["frontend/**"]
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# fe-codebase

Goal: a change that looks and works right from 760 to 1440 px, matches the design system, and is proven by tests
that read what the user sees.

## Where things live
- `src/components/designSystem/` holds shared UI and `src/components/app/` app-specific parts. Reuse before you build.
- `e2e/pages/*Page.ts` page objects own selectors and flows; specs in `e2e/pr/` only orchestrate, in Given/When/Then steps.
- Unit tests live in `test/unit/` (Vitest, happy-dom); `@r` points at `src/`.

## Signs to look deeper
- A table or form that also lives in a slide-in panel: use `@container` with `@md:`/`@lg:`, not window breakpoints.
- A new data fetch: useQuery, not useResult; check the loading, empty and error states.
- A test that finds elements by class name: use test IDs, ARIA roles or visible text, or a Storybook story per state.
- Code near the RSC boundary, dates and time zones, or global CSS: read references/risky-areas.md.

Run `npm run verify` before you say done (verify skill).

title: [Guilds] Write the be-codebase skill and its evals
needs: G7: the API test layer (tests_api/, fakes) once it lands; G5: the BE routines load this skill
what: The BE guild writes be-codebase in the be-guild plugin as the short entry point over the moved be-module-* skills: Django and DRF patterns, permissions, migrations and lock risk, API schema and SDK back-compat, the cloud and client gRPC contract, Celery, fakes over mocks, and the risky areas, with 3–10 eval cases.
why: BE bug and CI fixers need one entry point that says what matters here and when to read the deeper module guides. Evals show whether it helps compared with no plugin.
how: be-codebase stays short and sends the agent to be-module-cloud, be-module-client or be-module-sdk for depth, so the module guides load only when needed.
Signs to look deeper: a migration on a big table, a proto change, a serializer the SDK uses, a Celery task signature, a permission check, the client's raw (PHI) database.

Eval cases as case.yaml (sketch below): a model change mentions makemigrations --check and lock risk; a proto change keeps old fields; a serializer change checks SDK use; it stays quiet on a frontend task. pr-tagged cases use only free graders.
Point to G7's API test layer once it lands; until then the Django runner and the factories.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/plugins/be-guild/evals/be-codebase/proto-change/case.yaml
schema_version: "1.1"
name: be-codebase-proto-change
tags: [nightly, be-codebase] # has an llm grader, so it runs nightly, not on every PR
execution:
  prompt: >
    In fcp I need the on-prem client to send the cloud a new "disk_free_bytes" value with its heartbeat.
    The messages are in common/fcp_common/rhinoAgentRpc. Tell me what to change and what to watch out for.
  allowed_tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]
  max_turns: 200 # the eval tool's ceiling; a turn cap shouldn't decide the score
  timeout_seconds: 3600
context:
  add_dirs: [fixture] # a trimmed copy of the protos and handlers; no customer data
graders:
  - name: skill-fired
    type: tool_used
    tool: Skill
    input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?be-codebase"'
  - name: names-protoc
    type: regex
    pattern: "make protoc"
  - name: back-compat
    type: llm
    criteria: >
      PASS if the answer adds a new field instead of changing existing ones, says clients already installed at
      customers must keep working, and says to regenerate and commit the _pb2 files. FAIL if it renames or removes a field.

title: [Platform] Eval gate: claude plugin eval with pinned models in plugin CI
needs: G0: an evals key at the LLM gateway; G1: the eval results store; G1/G3: an ARC runner set inside inf that can reach the gateway
what: Run each changed plugin's eval suite in CI with pinned models: on PRs the cases tagged pr (free graders only), nightly every case including LLM-judge graders. Fail below 0.8, and fail when the plugin does worse than no plugin.
why: A skill can read well and still make results worse. Running every case three times with and without the plugin shows whether it helps before it reaches every laptop and agent.
how: Add the evals job (sketch below) to plugin-ci.yml, plus a nightly schedule (cron `23 2 * * *`) that runs every plugin and every case.

Runner: an ARC runner set inside inf with single-use pods, because the LLM gateway is internal. The runner holds no Anthropic key; ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at the gateway, which adds the evals key. Install bubblewrap and socat in the runner image for cases that grant Bash.
Pin the agent model (claude-opus-5-5, medium effort) and the judge (claude-sonnet-5-5 for rubrics), so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression.
`--trust-plugin` is acceptable here because the pod is single-use and holds nothing but gateway access; plugin hooks run outside the eval sandbox.
No --max-cost-usd: cost is reported (costUsd in the JSON) and charted in Grafana; a ceiling comes only after 4 weeks of data. Results go to the G1 eval store.

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.github/workflows/plugin-ci.yml (continued)
  evals:
    needs: validate
    if: needs.validate.outputs.changed_plugins != '[]'
    runs-on: ai-agents-runner-set # ARC set inside inf that can reach the LLM gateway; name from G1/G3, confirm
    strategy:
      matrix:
        plugin: ${{ fromJson(needs.validate.outputs.changed_plugins) }} # nightly: every plugin
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.LLM_GATEWAY_URL }} # the gateway adds the evals key; the runner holds none
      CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL: medium
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5 # pin by SHA
      - run: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.289
      - name: Run the cases with and without the plugin (3 runs each)
        run: |
          tags=$([ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "schedule" ] || echo "--tag pr") # PRs: free graders only
          claude plugin eval "plugins/${{ matrix.plugin }}" $tags \
            --trust-plugin --no-publish --json results.json \
            --model claude-opus-5-5 --judge-model claude-sonnet-5-5 \
            --threshold 0.8 --runs 3 -j 4
      - name: Fail if the plugin makes results worse than no plugin
        run: |
          jq -e '.aggregates.meanDelta == null or .aggregates.meanDelta >= 0' results.json \
            || { echo "::error::${{ matrix.plugin }} scores lower with the plugin than without it"; exit 1; }
          jq -r '.cases[] | select((.aggregates.delta // 0) < 0) | "::warning::\(.name) regressed by \(.aggregates.delta)"' results.json
      - name: Store results in the eval store (G1; AWS access through G1's OIDC role)
        if: always()
        run: aws s3 cp results.json "s3://${{ vars.EVAL_RESULTS_BUCKET }}/skill-evals/${{ matrix.plugin }}/${{ github.run_id }}.json"

title: [DevOps] Write the devops-codebase and infra-change skills and their evals
needs: G7: the DevOps checks (validate, tflint, trivy, kubeconform, actionlint) and CI plans
what: DevOps writes two skills in devops-guild: devops-codebase (the Terragrunt trees and modules, Helm and Argo CD structure, environments, naming, which checks run where, who to ask) and infra-change (checks without cloud keys, plans from CI, blast radius and rollback notes, never apply, destroy or sync), with eval cases.
why: The DevOps routines and anyone touching infrastructure need the map and the habits. The walls (no apply, no cloud keys) are enforced by infrastructure, so the skill explains the why and the safe path.
how: devops-codebase: the old multi_tenant/ tree (root.hcl) and the new terraform/ tree for new accounts such as ai-agents; module refs; the n8n pattern for inf tools; gitops' argocd-apps chart (product clusters only); Vault paths; naming (ai-agents for AI, rhino-agent for client VMs).
infra-change (sketch below): the checks to run, where the plan comes from, and the notes every infra PR needs.
Eval cases: a VPC change gets a blast-radius note; "just apply it" is declined with the safe path; a gitops values change names the environments it hits; it stays quiet for a frontend task.
Owner: DevOps (catalog.yaml).

code.text:
---
name: infra-change
description: "Use for any change in the infrastructure or gitops repos or in workflow files: the checks to run without cloud keys, how to get a plan, and the blast-radius and rollback notes every infra PR needs. A person applies; agents never apply, destroy or sync."
when_to_use: "Editing terragrunt.hcl, modules/, Helm values, Argo CD apps, Packer images or .github/workflows; asked to 'deploy', 'apply' or 'roll out'."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# infra-change

Goal: a reviewer can see what this changes, where, and how to undo it, before anyone applies it.

## Checks that need no cloud keys
`tofu fmt -check -recursive`, `terragrunt hcl format --check`, `terragrunt validate` on the units you touched, then
tflint, `trivy config .` and checkov. For gitops: `helm lint` and `helm template | kubeconform`. For workflows:
actionlint and zizmor.

## The plan
The plan comes from CI with a read-only role, or a person runs it over VPN and pastes it into the PR. You don't run
apply, destroy, argocd sync or workflow_dispatch; if the task seems to need one, stop and hand it to DevOps with
what you found.

## In every PR
- Blast radius: which accounts, clusters and environments change, and whether anything is replaced or deleted.
- Rollback: the revert, and what a revert doesn't undo (data, DNS, IAM).
- Look deeper when the plan shows a destroy or replace, IAM or security groups, state moves, or the shared inf cluster.

title: [Shai] Training 1: checks before code, proof not claims
what: A 45-minute hands-on session for all engineers on the verify habit: choose the checks before coding, plant a bug to prove a check can fail, and record proof for the PR.
why: The skills help only if people use the habit. Starting with checks and proof makes both human and agent PRs easier to review.
how: Prepare one FE and one BE exercise on seed data in FCP Lab: a small real bug from Jira, already fixed on a branch.
Show a PR written with proof next to one written with claims; let people plant a bug and watch a weak test still pass.
Record it; put the slides and recording in Drive "Rhino Team/Engineering" and link them from a brain page.
Turn the 3 questions people struggled with into eval cases for verify.

title: [Shai] Weekly office hours, with the Harness Lab course as self-study
what: A 30-minute weekly drop-in from W6 to W12 for questions about skills, plugins and agents, and the Harness Lab course offered as self-study.
why: People get stuck on small things, like a skill that doesn't fire or a plugin that won't install. A fixed slot unblocks them fast and shows us what to fix in the tools.
how: Book a recurring 30-minute slot (Shai and Platform alternate) and post a reminder in a public engineering channel.
Keep a log: question, answer, and whether it should become a skill line, an eval case or a brain page (most should).
Share Harness Lab (the 20-chapter course) as self-study with a suggested order, linked from the brain.
Report the top 3 themes in the weekly run review.

title: [Platform] Roll out rhino-core with managed settings and an MCP allow-list
needs: G0 (Fable off, agent teams off) and G1 (telemetry env) keys live in the same managed settings; G6-13: the compliance connector URL; G3: the agent image seeds the same plugins (CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_SEED_DIR) and carries the same policy file
what: Add the plugin and MCP keys to our Claude Code managed settings: only our marketplaces, the rhino marketplace at ref stable, rhino-core on for everyone, and approved MCP servers by URL, next to the Fable block and telemetry settings from G0 and G1.
why: Managed settings are the one way to give every engineer the same tested tools without asking each person to install them, and to keep unreviewed marketplaces and MCP servers off company laptops.
how: Inventory first: on 5 laptops run `claude mcp list` and `/plugin`, and list the claude.ai connectors people use (Jira, Slack, Figma), because allowedMcpServers also filters claude.ai connectors.

Decide with Ronen: keep anthropics/claude-plugins-official (people use figma and frontend-design from it); Rhino MCP on mcp-dev3 only, since prod reaches customer data and PHI never enters a prompt; the compliance connector from G6-13.

Decide the delivery with DevOps: the claude.ai admin console (one policy for the whole org, Owner role) or Fleet MDM profiles (lets pilots get a second profile with rhino-latest). Force-enabled plugins can't be swapped per person, so pilots need their own profile.
Merge the keys (sketch below) into the one policy (Platform is its single writer). Pilot on 3 people for 2 days: `/status` shows the managed source and `/plugin` lists rhino-core. Then everyone.
Agents: the G3 image bakes the stable catalog into a seed folder and the same policy file, so Nova runs what people run. Retire the claude.ai org copies of ticket-to-pr and fcp-lab.

title: [Shai] Training 2: plan mode and the grill
what: A hands-on session on planning before code: plan mode in Claude Code, the plan-and-grill skill, when to ask the requester first, and how to write checks the reviewer can trust.
why: A good plan with agreed checks is the cheapest point to catch a misread ticket, for people and for Nova.
how: Use two real tickets: a vague one (the grill asks questions first) and a small clear one (straight to a plan).
Pairs write a plan with plan mode and the skill, then swap and review each other's checks and edge cases.
Show the same plan format Nova posts in Jira and Slack, so people know what they will approve.
Record it, link it from the brain, and add the weak plans people wrote as eval cases for plan-and-grill.

title: [Guilds] Write the fix-bug, fix-ci and fix-flaky-test skills with evals
needs: G5: the bug, CI and flaky-test fixers load these, and their ROUTINE-BENCH slices re-run on every change
what: The guilds write three task skills: fix-bug (triage, reproduce first, root cause with file:line, smallest fix, regression test, look nearby), fix-ci (is main red too, fingerprint, code/test/environment/flaky, smallest fix, hand environment problems to DevOps) and fix-flaky-test (reproduce the flake, usual causes, fix the cause, about 50 green runs).
why: The bug fixers are the most important routines, and people follow the same steps. The result checks (no skipped or deleted tests) are enforced elsewhere; these skills teach the method.
how: fix-bug and fix-ci go in rhino-core (owners: FE and BE guilds, Platform); fix-flaky-test goes in be-guild.
Write each with worked examples from real past tickets, on seed data, and the signs to look deeper (sketch below).
fix-flaky-test: reproduce with repeats, random order, fixed seeds and parallel runs; the usual causes (timing, shared state, order, time zones, network); fix the cause, never with retries or sleeps.
Eval cases per skill: does it fire, does it reproduce before fixing, does it refuse to skip a test, does it hand an environment failure to DevOps with evidence.

code.text:
---
name: fix-bug
description: "Use when the task is a reported bug: triage it, reproduce it first with a failing test or a recorded browser run on seed data, find the root cause with file:line, make the smallest safe fix, add a regression test, and look for the same pattern nearby."
when_to_use: "A Jira Bug ticket, a bug report in Slack, 'this is broken', 'X shows the wrong value'."
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---
# fix-bug

Goal: a fix for the cause, not the symptom, proven by a test that failed before and passes after.

1. Triage: is it a duplicate (search Jira), which team owns it, how bad is it for users?
2. Reproduce first, at the level the user sees it: an API test for BE, a component or Playwright test for FE, or a
   recorded browser run on seed data in FCP Lab. Keep the reproduction.
3. If it won't reproduce, stop and report what you tried, on which data and commit, and ask the reporter one
   specific question. That report is useful on its own.
4. Root cause: name the file:line and why it happened (the wrong assumption, not only the line).
5. The smallest safe fix: the reproduction now passes and the rest of verify stays green.
6. Look nearby: the same pattern elsewhere? List the places in the PR; fix them only if the ticket covers them.

title: [Guilds] Write the remaining task skills and security-fix, with evals
needs: G5: the routines that use these; Ronen reviews security-fix
what: Write upgrade-dependency, remove-dead-code, add-tests, merge-duplicates and small-feature (guilds), and security-fix (DevOps, with Ronen), each short with 3–10 eval cases.
why: These cover the rest of the routines' work and everyday tasks. Short skills with evals are easy to trim later if they don't help.
how: upgrade-dependency: changelog and migration guide first, search our usage, codemods, one package at a time, run the flows that use it, note the risks. remove-dead-code: candidates from knip (FE) or vulture (BE); prove each one unused (dynamic imports, strings, SDK and public exports, feature flags); small batches; deletions only.

add-tests: untested behaviour on changed lines, the right level, each new test fails on a planted bug, readable names, no snapshot dumps. merge-duplicates: real duplication or coincidence, one abstraction, no behaviour change. small-feature: reviewable slices, flags when needed, every screen state.
security-fix: is it reachable, is a fixed version out, the upgrade path, base-image rebuilds, the scanner before and after, a link to the finding.
Each skill gets at least one negative case: an unrelated request must not load it (sketch below).

code.text:
# RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/plugins/rhino-core/evals/remove-dead-code/stays-quiet-on-feature/case.yaml
schema_version: "1.1"
name: remove-dead-code-stays-quiet-on-feature
description: An unrelated feature request must not load remove-dead-code.
tags: [pr, remove-dead-code] # free graders only, so it runs on every PR
execution:
  prompt: "Add a 'Last updated' column to the datasets table in the dashboard, newest first."
  allowed_tools: [Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]
  max_turns: 200 # the eval tool's ceiling
graders:
  - name: does-not-fire
    type: tool_used
    tool: Skill
    input_match: '"skill"\s*:\s*"(?:[\w-]+:)?remove-dead-code"'
    min: 0
    max: 0
    arm: both # score it in both arms; a Skill grader is otherwise only an indicator

title: [Platform] Training 3: many agents at once, sized and given a token budget
what: A hands-on session on running several agents at once: worktrees, background agents and dynamic workflows; scout first, try a small slice, then give a workflow a size and a token budget in the prompt.
why: Many agents help when the work splits into independent, checkable pieces and hurt on step-by-step work; one review once started 221 agents and burned about 47M tokens. People should know when to fan out and how to keep it sane.
how: Exercises in fcp: two tickets in two worktrees; a background agent running tests; a read-only review workflow with lenses and a skeptic per finding; a sized prompt such as "audit unused exports in frontend/src, about 10 agents, +300k".
Teach the rule: one writer per change; fan out for research, review and tests; stay with one agent for a chain of dependent steps.
Show /usage and the status line, so each person sees their own spend. No new per-person caps; Anthropic's defaults stay.
Record it, link it from the brain, and turn the questions into eval cases or brain pages.

title: [Platform] Training 4: working with Nova
needs: G4: the Nova pilot is live (Jira assignment, the Slack app, draft PRs)
what: A session on handing work to Nova: assigning a ticket, the readiness check and grill questions, approving a plan in Slack, answering questions, reviewing its draft PRs and stopping a run.
why: Nova helps only if people give it good tickets and review its PRs well. The requester never approves the PR, so every reviewer needs to know what to look for.
how: Walk one pilot ticket end to end on seed data: assign to Nova, the plan in Slack, Approve / Change / Stop, the draft PR with proof, Byte's review, and approval by someone other than the requester.
Show how to read the PR story, the checks table and the receipt, and what a scope-judge veto looks like.
Say when not to use Nova: vague work with no owner, or anything that needs production data.
Record it and add an FAQ page to the brain.
